battle.title: Key Master
battle.description: Primary, foreign and unique keys plus constraint behaviour.

questions.text: Which statement about a PRIMARY KEY is true?
options: A table may have several primary keys
It uniquely identifies each row and cannot contain NULL
It may contain duplicates if the other columns differ
It is always a single auto-increment number
questions.answer: It uniquely identifies each row and cannot contain NULL
questions.explanation: A primary key must be unique and non-NULL, and a table has exactly one, though it can span several columns. It is not necessarily numeric or auto-generated.

questions.text: You must guarantee that every orders.customer_id refers to a customer that really exists. Which constraint do you add?
options: CHECK (customer_id > 0)
UNIQUE on customer_id
FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id)
NOT NULL on customer_id
questions.explanation: A foreign key makes the database reject values that have no matching parent row. CHECK > 0 only tests a number's range, UNIQUE would forbid a customer having two orders, and NOT NULL only forbids missing values.

questions.text: users(id PRIMARY KEY, email UNIQUE) holds (1, 'a@x'). Then three separate statements run on PostgreSQL or MySQL InnoDB: INSERT (2, 'a@x'); INSERT (3, NULL); INSERT (4, NULL). A failed statement changes nothing. What does the table hold at the end?
options: 3 rows: ids 1, 3, 4
2 rows: ids 1, 3
4 rows: ids 1, 2, 3, 4
1 row: id 1, because all inserts fail
questions.explanation: The first insert repeats 'a@x' and violates UNIQUE. NULL is not considered equal to another NULL, so both NULL inserts succeed in these databases, leaving ids 1, 3 and 4.

questions.text: orders.customer_id references customers(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE. What happens when a customer row is deleted?
options: The delete is rejected while orders exist
The orders keep their customer_id as orphans
The orders' customer_id is set to NULL
The customer's orders are deleted automatically too
questions.answer: The customer's orders are deleted automatically too
questions.explanation: CASCADE propagates the delete to the child rows. Rejecting the delete is RESTRICT or NO ACTION, setting NULL is SET NULL, and leaving orphans is exactly what a foreign key prevents.

questions.text: A table (id, email, name) has both id and email unique and never NULL. Which statement is correct?
options: Both id and email are candidate keys, and one of them is chosen as the primary key
Only id can be a key because email is text
email must be turned into a composite key with name
A table needs a surrogate key even when it has candidate keys
questions.answer: Both id and email are candidate keys, and one of them is chosen as the primary key
questions.explanation: Any minimal set of columns that uniquely identifies rows is a candidate key. The primary key is simply the candidate key you choose, and the others remain as UNIQUE constraints. Data type does not stop a column from being a key.
